_doc: LIVING REGISTRY of candidate metrics for VIDEO-derived dynamism.
Purpose: today the reactive energy is 100% audio (max stem envelope per frame).
The video edit is itself danceable/dynamic — so energy should also read the PICTURE.
This file collects metric ideas; the processor (compute_visual_dynamism.py) implements the
ones marked IMPLEMENTED and writes a per-frame signal (visual-dynamism.json).
NOTHING here is wired into the artwork yet — this is exploration until one proves reliable.
Reusable: the same frame_metrics() runs on a single image too (for scoring stills later).
goal: A per-frame 0..1 'how much is going on in this frame' signal, from the pixels.
eventual_use: Blend into scene energy / field intensity ALONGSIDE audio (e.g. energy = max(audioEnv, k*visualDynamism)).
Could also drive RGB-split amount, morph rate, particle density — the busier the frame, the wilder the field.
User will later run the same metric against a folder of still images to rank them.

ideas.name: grid differentiation (spatial 'mind-fuck' density)
ideas.author: user
ideas.hypothesis: A busy/trippy frame has many distinct, high-contrast regions; a calm frame is flat and uniform.
ideas.method: Split each frame into a GRID (default 10x10). Per cell compute within-cell luminance contrast (texture) and within-cell colour spread (palette). Aggregate two ways: (a) BUSYNESS = mean cell contrast (how textured cells are on average); (b) DIFFERENTIATION = spread of cell MEANS across the grid (how different one region is from another — 'different palettes on different squares').
ideas.notes: grid_diff is the closest to the user's 'different palettes on different squares'. grid_busyness is 'items per cell'.

ideas.name: temporal motion (danceability)
ideas.hypothesis: Danceable footage MOVES — frame-to-frame change is the most direct dynamism cue.
ideas.method: Mean absolute luminance difference between consecutive sampled frames.
ideas.notes: Cheap (one previous-frame buffer). Spikes hard at cuts — may want to separate 'cut spikes' from 'sustained motion' later.

ideas.name: global colourfulness (Hasler-Susstrunk)
ideas.hypothesis: Saturated, varied palettes read as more alive than muted/monochrome ones.
ideas.method: Standard opponent-channel colourfulness: rg=R-G, yb=0.5(R+G)-B; C = sqrt(std_rg^2+std_yb^2) + 0.3*sqrt(mean_rg^2+mean_yb^2).

ideas.name: global contrast
ideas.method: Whole-frame luminance standard deviation. Reference channel; complements grid_busyness.

ideas.name: edge density (Sobel/Laplacian)
ideas.method: Gradient magnitude per pixel, averaged. 'How many edges' proxy. numpy-only via np.gradient or a 3x3 kernel.
ideas.why_deferred: grid_busyness already captures texture cheaply; add if we want finer edge sensitivity.

ideas.name: palette entropy / unique-colour count
ideas.method: Quantise colours (e.g. 4 bits/channel) and measure histogram entropy or count of populated bins. High entropy = rich palette.
ideas.why_interesting: Directly answers 'how many different colours/palettes are present'.

ideas.name: per-cell spectral energy (FFT high-freq)
ideas.method: 2D FFT per cell, ratio of high-frequency to total energy = detail/'chaos' density. More rigorous 'mind-fuck' measure than std.

ideas.name: optical-flow magnitude
ideas.method: Dense optical flow between frames; mean vector magnitude = true motion (not just pixel diff). Distinguishes camera move / dancing from flicker.

ideas.name: reuse scene-cut spikes
ideas.method: The ffmpeg scene_score we already bake is per-frame change; could feed a 'cut intensity' channel directly. Free — already computed.

combining.note: The processor outputs each channel SEPARATELY plus a provisional 'dynamism' blend, so weights can change WITHOUT re-processing the video.
combining.todo: Correlate each channel against the audio energy — keep the channels that add NEW information (low correlation), drop redundant ones.

open_questions: Should dynamism ADD to audio energy (union of busy) or MODULATE it (audio gates, video colours)?
Sustained motion vs cut-spike: separate channels?

Normalize per-video (min-max over the song) or with a fixed absolute scale (so different videos compare)? Currently per-video; fixed scale needed for cross-image ranking (idea: store raw stats to allow both).
